Hey team - quick answers we can send back to FinApps. Keeping these high-level but actionable: 

1) Auth / Private VPC
- Recommendation: OIDC short-lived JWTs issued by FinApps IdP, validated by Redwood. For Private VPC connectors, we support mTLS as an option for additional mutual-auth; common pattern is OIDC for session-level auth + mTLS for connection-level trust.
- Exchange pattern: FinApps issues access token to the client; client presents token to Redwood SDK. For server-to-server calls inside Private, we recommend short TTL tokens (1-5m) and automatic refresh in SDK.

2) JSON Schema validation & rejection policy
- Redwood supports pluggable validators (JSON Schema). You can configure per-tool:
  * reject - call fails if schema mismatch (good for payments/destructive ops)
  * sanitize - attempt to coerce/clean and return with warnings
  * human-review - queue to an operator review flow (we can wire to your ticketing system)
- Default recommend: reject for any tool that issues state changes; sanitize or warn for read-only enrichment tools.

3) Parallel tools and failure semantics
- Pattern: fan-out the model call to multiple tool adapters (enrichment, compliance). Use an aggregator that waits for N of M results or a timeout window.
- Recommended semantics:
  * Compliance-check: strict - if it fails/timeout, block the action and return a structured refusal with an explainable reason.
  * Enrichment: best-effort - return partial results and mark fields as best-effort.
- We support a configurable policy engine: sequential, parallel-await-all, parallel-await-any, and fallback chains.

4) Embeddings residency & KMS
- Option A (hosted): Redwood stores encrypted embeddings; customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) supported so Redwood cannot read raw vectors.
- Option B (private): embeddings stored in your VPC/on-prem store; Redwood inference can call a local retriever via the private connector at low-latency.
- Recommendation: If PII risk is high, choose Option B or hosted with BYOK and strict access controls/audit logs.

5) Example tool definition (pseudo-JSON) - include in reply to customer:
{"name": "get_account_summary", "type": "http", "method": "POST", "endpoint": "https://api.finapps.internal/v1/account/summary", "auth": "oidc", "response_schema": "/schemas/account_summary.json", "failure_policy": "reject"}

6) Error handling patterns
- Best practice: return structured errors with stable error codes and remediation hints. Retry policies should be idempotent-aware (avoid retrying destructive ops).
- Timeouts: prefer short model-compute timeouts + longer tool timeouts with clear user-facing messaging.

Happy to expand any section in the technical deep-dive. I can also prep a short demo repo that wires an SDK snippet, tool mocks, and a small local retriever for embeddings.

Hi Priya / Alex -

Thanks for the questions - see concise answers from our solutions team below (copied). Key points:
- Auth: OIDC short-lived tokens recommended; mTLS available for Private connector. SDK handles refresh.
- Schema validation: yes, configurable per-tool with reject / sanitize / human-review policies. We recommend reject for payments.
- Parallel tools: use policy engine; recommend fail-fast for compliance, best-effort for enrichment.
- Embeddings: you can keep vectors in your VPC or use BYOK in hosted mode.
